# Symbolic Engineering

> Symbolic Engineering builds Contour, a reasoning platform for the databases a company already has. Databases and data warehouses record what happened; they do not record what it means. Contour builds that missing description over the source systems a client already runs, and serves it to their team and their AI agents over the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Every result traces back to the records it came from.

Contour is domain-neutral. We have met the same problem across hedge funds, fintechs, healthcare and manufacturing: the organisation holds an enormous amount of data and has no affordable way to act on it, because organising it into something answerable is expensive and has to be paid for again with every new question. A fintech holds every transaction it has processed and cannot say which segments its revenue comes from. A plant holds a signal per second from every sensor on the line and has no basis for choosing which asset to service before the next outage.

Profiles that recur commercially include investment firms holding decades of positions, filings, counterparty records and market data across systems that were never designed to reconcile; process or discrete manufacturers whose lines are instrumented end to end and whose maintenance intervals are still set by the calendar rather than by any particular asset's own history; and hospitals whose planned maintenance comes from manufacturers' intervals and whose criticality is discovered when something fails. These are examples of where the same structure applies rather than the limit of it.

Company: Symbolic Engineering. Product: Contour.
Operating regions: Europe, North America, Brazil.
Contact: contact@symbolic.engineering

## Method

We build the structured model before placing any reasoning layer on top of it. The problem with pointing a language model at a warehouse is not the query language: it is that a schema records what happened without recording what it means, so the model must infer the meaning. It infers correctly most of the time, and the incorrect results are indistinguishable from the correct ones, so they propagate into decisions before anyone catches them. Engagements therefore begin with the client's source systems, and the model is validated against records the client already trusts. We read from those systems; we do not modify them.

## What Contour is not

Contour is not a rule engine, and the distinction is structural rather than a matter of degree. A rule engine is reactive: it holds conditions and the actions that follow them, and it fires when incoming facts match, so its knowledge lives in the rules and its output is a firing. Contour is declarative and queried. It expresses a model of the business, covering entities, the relationships between them, and the metrics defined over them, as a semantic layer over the source systems the client already runs. Nothing in it fires; it is asked and it answers. A rule engine accumulates logic; Contour maintains a description that can be validated against records the client already trusts. Nor is Contour a text-to-SQL tool, a BI dashboard, or a replacement for the client's historian, warehouse or maintenance system: it reads from those and adds structure over them.

## Product

- [Product overview](https://symbolic.engineering/product/): The platform continuously processes source systems into one governed model and exposes it to analysts and the AI tools they already use. Declarative and queried, not reactive: it holds no conditions or actions.
- [Model Context Layer](https://symbolic.engineering/product/model-context-layer/): Exposes the structured model to AI assistants over the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Contour does not generate SQL with a language model; it exposes a constrained set of typed, tested operations over a governed semantic model, and the assistant composes those operations. Correctness is therefore a property of versioned platform code rather than of the model's guess. Access is read-only, entitlements are enforced at the interface, and every result carries lineage back to source.
- [Asset Tree & Failure Propagation](https://symbolic.engineering/product/failure-propagation/): Models a plant as a directed dependency graph rather than a flat asset register, traces how one component failure cascades downstream, and derives criticality from the graph so it updates as the plant changes.
- [Reliability Engineering](https://symbolic.engineering/product/reliability-engineering/): Fits hazard models to each asset's own failure and maintenance history and reports remaining useful life as a distribution, so assets can be ranked by probability of failure within a chosen planning window and by expected consequence.
- [Sensor Intelligence](https://symbolic.engineering/product/sensor-intelligence/): Ingests instrumentation continuously and resolves tags to the equipment they measure, collapsing correlated alarms into single events and surfacing sensor drift before it contaminates downstream models.

## Use cases

- **Investment firm**: the firm runs a data lake or warehouse and employs DBAs who can query all of it, yet the questions that matter still take days and several people. An AI assistant pointed straight at the warehouse returns fluent, confident and incorrect figures, so nobody trusts it with a position. The client sends us its sources. Contour replicates them, resolves them into one structured model of the firm, and returns an endpoint the client's own assistant connects to. Analysts ask in plain language, answers are built from verified operations rather than generated queries, and every figure carries lineage back to source.
- **Process or discrete manufacturer**: the line is instrumented end to end, with each piece of equipment carrying its own measurement — a vessel measured for pressure and oxidation, an exhauster downstream measured for temperature, and so on along the train. Those instruments report continuously and the maintenance system holds years of work orders written against the same equipment, yet the interval on which any given asset is serviced still comes from the calendar, the manufacturer's manual or the last shutdown. Long-lead spares arrive late and planned work arrives as breakdown. Contour builds the asset tree of the line from the equipment master the client already maintains, in SAP or wherever it lives, attaches each instrument to the equipment it measures, and fits each asset's own failure and maintenance history with established reliability statistics conditioned on what its instruments have been reporting. The result is a preventive maintenance window for that specific asset, carrying the probability behind the date and the records the estimate was built from.
- **Hospital clinical engineering**: the hospital carries several thousand devices against a planned maintenance schedule taken almost entirely from manufacturers' intervals. The schedule states what is due; it does not state what a failure would cost, so consequence is discovered rather than anticipated and capital replacement is argued from equipment age. Contour builds the dependency graph of the estate from the equipment register, the building management system and the service history written against both, derives criticality from that graph rather than from a hand-maintained column, and reports each asset with both its probability of failure and the clinical services it would take with it. Manufacturers' intervals and accreditation requirements remain the floor; what changes is where attention and capital go above it. The case requires no patient data.

## Key definitions

- **Asset tree**: a structured representation of how equipment in a facility depends on other equipment, built from maintenance records, process topology and control system configuration.
- **Failure propagation analysis**: tracing how the failure of one component spreads through the equipment that depends on it, following consequence downstream to the production output affected.
- **Remaining useful life (RUL)**: an estimate of how much service an asset has left before likely failure, expressed as a distribution rather than a single date.
- **Sensor drift**: gradual divergence of an instrument's readings from the true value it measures, dangerous because the output continues to look valid.
- **Semantic layer**: a description of a business placed over its source systems, covering the entities that exist, how they relate, and the metrics defined over them, against which questions are asked and answered. It is queried rather than triggered, which is what separates it from a rule engine.
- **Closed world assumption**: the model answers only what it describes. A question falling outside it returns a refusal rather than an inferred figure, which is why a wrong answer becomes an admission of ignorance instead of a plausible number.
- **Model Context Protocol (MCP)**: an open standard for connecting AI assistants to external systems and data sources. Contour ships an MCP server over the structured model, so any client that speaks the protocol, whether Claude, an internal agent or a desktop assistant, can query the business without being tied to a model vendor.
